species.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent; frequently cultivated in tropical streets and parks.
species.ecology: Tree of tropical forest and seasonally dry tropical habitats; it is also frequently cultivated elsewhere in the tropics.
species.short_notes: A large strangling fig with leathery leaves and aerial roots that can develop into additional trunks.

knowledge.text: Banyan is a large strangling fig native to the Indian subcontinent. Aerial roots hang from its branches and can develop into additional trunks, while its leathery leaves have prominent lateral veins.
Banyan occurs in tropical forest and is frequently cultivated elsewhere in the tropics; Kew's species profile describes it as not threatened.

species.native_status: Native range includes India from southeast Pakistan to Myanmar.
species.conservation_status: Not assessed in this starter record
species.ecology: Tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome with environmental and social uses.
species.short_notes: Also called peepal; the heart-shaped leaf and long tapering tip are useful field characters, but a single leaf view may be insufficient.

knowledge.text: The native range of sacred fig extends from southeast Pakistan to Myanmar and includes India, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
Sacred fig is a tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome and is recorded by Kew with environmental and social uses.

species.native_status: Native range is southwestern India; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
species.conservation_status: Not assessed in this starter record
species.ecology: Tree of the wet tropical biome with flowers and fruit borne on the main branches and trunk.
species.short_notes: A crop and food tree from southwestern India. Fruit, bark, leaves, and whole-plant views can differ substantially.

knowledge.text: Jackfruit has a native range in southwestern India and is now widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Jackfruit is a tree; Kew records its inflorescences on the main branches and trunk and records the species as having food and environmental uses.

species.native_status: Native range includes India and tropical and subtropical Asia; commonly grown in South Asian homes.
species.ecology: Perennial or subshrub of the seasonally dry tropical biome; often cultivated.
species.short_notes: Also called tulsi. Its aromatic foliage and small flowers are useful context, but cultivated forms can vary in colour.

knowledge.text: Holy basil is an aromatic perennial or subshrub with elliptic leaves and small brown nutlets; it is closely related to culinary basil.
Holy basil is native to tropical and subtropical Asia, is cultivated in other tropical areas, and is described by Kew as widespread and least concern.

species.native_status: Native to northern India and Pakistan; now widely cultivated in the tropics.
species.conservation_status: Least concern (IUCN Red List assessment recorded by Kew)
species.ecology: Small tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome, also grown widely in cultivated and artificial habitats.
species.short_notes: Also called moringa. Feathery leaves, pale flowers, and long ribbed pods are distinctive views to collect when available.

knowledge.text: Moringa is native to northern India and Pakistan and is now widely cultivated throughout the tropics.
The starter catalog records Moringa oleifera as LC — Least Concern using the IUCN Red List assessment linked in this record.

species.native_status: Native range extends from Bhutan to India; cultivated widely for its fragrant flowers.
species.conservation_status: Not assessed in this starter record
species.ecology: Scrambling shrub of the seasonally dry tropical biome; also recorded in cultivated and artificial habitats.
species.short_notes: A fragrant jasmine with white flowers. Flower and leaf views are more informative than a distant garden scene.

knowledge.text: Arabian jasmine has a native range from Bhutan to India and is introduced or cultivated in many tropical regions.
Arabian jasmine is a scrambling shrub that grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

species.native_status: Native to Kerala and Tamil Nadu in India.
species.ecology: Tree native to the seasonally dry tropical biome in the southern Western Ghats range recorded by Kew.
species.short_notes: A region-specific catalog entry included to make conservation context visible; do not treat a low-confidence image match as a confirmed record.

knowledge.text: Syzygium microphyllum has a native range in India, specifically Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
The starter catalog records Syzygium microphyllum as EN — Endangered using the linked IUCN Red List assessment.
